messages:
alex: FYI I'm seeing a mem growth regression on prod when clients send very long contexts with continuous batching. Seems correlated with spikes in KV pages allocated during batch merges.

maria: saw a few alerts earlier, footprint jumped ~20% over 30m on node pool A. Any profiling yet? :thinking_face: 

alex: uploaded a short perf dump to the profiling bucket: gs://redwood-perf/kvcache/175820/merge-fanout-1.pbz2. Top lines show repeated page allocs + copies when batches are merged.

perf-bot: New profile available: gs://redwood-perf/kvcache/175820/merge-fanout-1.pbz2 (flamegraph + allocation timeline).

chris: hypothesis: when continuous-batcher merges requests with different prefixes we are duplicating KV pages instead of reusing references. Merge path currently does a shallow copy then patch -> ends up creating separate backing pages for each slot. That explodes memory on long contexts.

jess: that would also explain head-of-line stalls I saw: merge waits on first request kvcache lookup, other requests block waiting for merged KV to be materialized. If materialization does copies, it's slow.

maria: can you point to the code path? I remember a comment about a "safe copy" in kv_cache.cc that avoids aliasing across tenants.

chris: lines in runtime/kvcache/merge_handler.cpp around 248. The safe copy conservatively clones pages if refcount > 1, but our refcounts are wrong after split/merge operations so it overclones.

alex: small repro I ran locally (pseudo):
```
# spin up continuous-batcher with 64 small requests that share prefixes
for i in seq 1 64; do curl -X POST $SVC -d '{"prompt":"<common-prefix> token $i ..."}'; done
# watch /proc/<pid>/smaps and kvcache page counters
```
results: peak RSS +70MB vs baseline, and 200k extra page alloc events in the profile.

simon: thought: instead of copying on merge, can we switch to a copy-on-write indirection layer (shared page slab + small header per view)? That would let merged batches share pages until a write is needed. Avoids copies in read-only generation phase.

jess: COW sounds ideal but risky for now. We should first fix the refcount bug so "safe copy" actually is safe. Then add metrics for copy counts per merge.

chris: agreed. I reproduced the refcount mismatch: when split creates temp fragments, it never increments the parent page refcount on reattach. I'll open a small PR that fixes the increment and adds assert in debug builds.

alex: please also add a perf regression test that runs the 64-request merge scenario under load and checks for no >10% RSS increase.

chris: will do. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812 (WIP). Adds fix + unit tests + perf harness.

maria: any quick mitigation we can ship to prod before the fix? Maybe reduce max continuous-batch merge size to limit fanout (config knob).

jess: we can set max_merge_width down to 8 in fleet for now. That will increase QPS slightly but should stop the large cross-prefix merges that cause explosion. I'll roll a config patch. deploy-bot: schedule?

deploy-bot: Config rollout queued for staging (pods: runtime-a,b,c). Will schedule prod if staging passes.

alex: timeline: chris PR for refcount fix today, jess will roll config to staging, run perf harness, then prod if green. I'll follow up with postmortem draft.

maria: also capture KV fragmentation metrics: pages_allocated, pages_shared, copy_events per minute. Add tracing tags for merge_id so we can correlate.

chris: adding metrics + logs in PR too. Also adding a debug endpoint to dump merge graph for a request id. Use carefully.

jess: thanks all. Good catch. Assigning: chris (fix+tests), jess (config rollout + perf run), alex (postmortem + prod monitor), simon (design for COW follow-up).

alex: one more note: long-context growth still unusual even after merge limit — might be fragmentation due to small free slabs. Keep an eye.

maria: copied to #incidents and started incident thread for tracking. :white_check_mark:
